Work in /home/user/BookMinder on the current branch. Rewrite `.claude/skills/bookminder/references/apple-books-domain.md` from a list of numbered correction-entries into a domain MODEL that teaches a fresh agent how Apple Books stores a library on macOS. Read this brief fully first.

## The author's diagnosis (this session)
The current page (read it: it is B-40..B-59, bold headline + body per entry) was produced by mapping mined transcript corrections one-to-one into entries, using the conduct-skill format where the bold headline IS the rule. For domain knowledge that yields "calorie free" headlines and a page organized by the history of corrections instead of the structure of the storage. His words: "we are basically saying there is the P list and there is the SQL database, and we should be saying, what's in the P list, what's in the database, when to look where." He wants the page to teach the territory: "this resulting artifact feels wrong as something that you teach a fresh agent about how to work with Apple Books on disk."

Standing rulings that survive: imperative voice addressed to the agent with the why attached (skill-creator standard; no self-description, no discovery narration, no aphorisms); no verification stamps, no timestamps, no line numbers, no size figures, no environment sentences ("this environment has no live database"), never mention CLAUDE.md (the rules file is `AGENTS.md` when a fact needs it); unknowns stated as facts about ignorance; `docs/apple_books.md` untouched; doc pointers collected in ONE trailing "Further reading" map, not sprinkled per paragraph; never hard-wrap prose (one line per paragraph or bullet); the page is read whole, so optimize the whole, not per-item completeness; token economy is a goal — DRY.

## The transformation: model first, corrections second
1. Build the model. Structure the page by the storage's own structure, roughly: what exists on disk (the two containers, the plist, the BKLibrary sqlite, the AEAnnotation database only as far as the record knows it) → what each store holds and what it is authoritative for → when to read which → the library table's columns that matter, each with meaning, the predicate the code encodes, and its unknowns → the environment lifecycle (what exists on a machine in each user state) → working the database (query discipline). Prose paragraphs and short bullet lists under section headings; no numbered ids, no bold headline sentences. A short table is acceptable for a column-meaning map only if each row stays short (the author reads on a phone; a wide table renders as one endless line).
2. Fold every existing fact in at the point of the model where it applies. The current page's twenty entries are the CONTENT inventory; every fact, predicate, unknown, and governance constraint in them must land somewhere in the model (the cloud display-vs-filter divergence and its "change neither side without the author's direction and a spec" ruling; the `sort_by='updated'` removal; the fixture's NULL `ZISFINISHED`; the `!cloud` spec's vacuity; the ZTITLE duplicates; the composite sample predicate; the census method; the doc's standing and the author's doc-editing rules; all of it). Do not add facts you cannot verify in the tree; do not drop any.
3. Coverage test, mechanical: `.coordination/compile/rule-index-bookminder.md` maps mined rules to B-40..B-59 (read its domain rows and footer roster). After writing, walk B-40..B-59 one by one and confirm each has a home in the new page; list any that do not, and why, in your return. Then update the rule index's footer roster: replace the B-40..B-59 id lines with a mapping from each retired id to the new page's section heading (anchor) where its content now lives, so traceability survives without ids on the page.
4. Fix cross-references: grep `.claude/skills/bookminder/` for `B-4[0-9]`, `B-5[0-9]`, and for "the domain page" mentions; the current-state page's B-68 cites the domain page's cloud divergence, and the router's page-map line for the domain page must be re-derived from the new structure. `.coordination/apple-books-recon.md` keys its checklist by B-ids — re-key those items to the new section headings.
5. Verify code facts against `bookminder/apple_books/library.py` and the specs under `specs/apple_books/` (read them whole); verify fixture facts with a query through Python's sqlite3 module against the test_reader fixture (the `sqlite3` CLI is absent here). Never read anything under `claude-dev-log-diary/`.

## Deliverables, each committed as it lands (stage by name, never `git add .`; do not push)
- D1 the rewritten domain page
- D2 rule-index footer mapping
- D3 cross-reference fixes in SKILL.md, current-state page, recon brief
Run `python3 .claude/skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py .claude/skills/bookminder` before the final commit. End every commit message with:
```
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01233T9ME4hRqtMsmEqbGtbP
```

Max 12 lines: commits with one clause each; word count old vs new; the coverage walk result (ids without a home, if any); validator result; any fact you could not verify and how you stated it; any deviation from this brief and why.

1	# Apple Books domain
2	
3	Read the entry for any column, file, or container before writing code or a spec that touches it. Treat what a spec pins against the fixtures as established, and treat an entry that says "unknown" as a boundary, not a gap to fill by reasoning. Open `docs/apple_books.md` only when you need the evidence behind an entry: it is the territory map from the research spike, with screenshots and the discovery narrative; the map at the end names the section for each entry.
4	
5	## Data sources
6	
7	- **B-40 — Two containers, one glob.** Read `Books.plist` and the per-book `<asset-id>.epub` files from `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.BKAgentService/Data/Documents/iBooks/Books/`, and the library database from `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/`. Find the database by glob, `BKLibrary-*.sqlite`, never by literal name: the numeric segments in the file name differ per install.
8	- **B-41 — Read reading state from the database, not the plist.** `Books.plist` is a catalogue: each entry in its `Books` list carries `itemName`, `artistName`, `path`, and `updateDate`; its `BKPercentComplete` appears only on finished books, always 1.0, so it cannot express progress. Reading state lives in the table `ZBKLIBRARYASSET`: `ZREADINGPROGRESS` (0.0 to 1.0), `ZLASTOPENDATE`, `ZISFINISHED`, `ZDATEFINISHED`, `ZCREATIONDATE`. Treat the database as the authoritative catalogue too: titles the database knows can be missing from the plist, even from a fresh copy, for a reason never established, so never infer membership or cloud status from plist absence.
9	- **B-42 — Do not sort or filter on `updateDate`.** Its meaning is unverified, probably the publisher's revision date rather than reading activity. Take recency from `ZLASTOPENDATE`. A `sort_by='updated'` option was removed for this reason; do not reintroduce it without establishing the field's meaning.
10	- **B-43 — Never filter by on-disk file existence.** Books lazy-download from iCloud, so a library entry with no `.epub` on disk is a normal entry. Presence on disk is a download state, not a membership test; no code path stats a book file.
11	- **B-44 — Convert timestamps from the Apple epoch.** Database timestamps count seconds from 2001-01-01 UTC, not 1970; raw values look like plausible Unix times and come out about 31 years wrong if you treat them as such. Use `APPLE_EPOCH + timedelta(seconds=value)` as `library.py` does.
12	
13	## The library table and its columns
14	
15	- **B-45 — ZSTATE.** Use the mapping the code encodes: 1 = present locally (downloaded books and downloaded samples), 3 = cloud book, 6 = cloud sample not yet downloaded. Treat 5 as unmapped: it was seen on a series entity row and on unowned member titles sharing a `ZSERIESID`, no criterion for telling those apart was established, and the population is large. Treat "which values show a cloud icon" as unsettled: cloud-icon books were seen at 1, 3, and 6, but that observation paired an iPhone screenshot with the Mac's database, where one title can legitimately differ, so 1 may mean local on the queried machine only. When you take a census, enumerate every distinct value from the database first and characterize each; never reason from the UI toward values you already know.
16	- **B-46 — Detect samples with the composite predicate.** `is_sample` is `ZSTATE = 6 OR ZISSAMPLE = 1`, and the specs pin both halves. Never treat `ZISSAMPLE = 0` as proof of a full book: unmistakable samples carry 0 and are identifiable only by ZSTATE 6. Treat the lifecycle (a store sample enters as 6/0 and becomes 1/1 once opened) as a proposal, not an observation: it is inferred from one title flipping between queries, never from one row seen before and after. Re-run the query for any per-title value; never quote a title's state from notes.
17	- **B-47 — Leave the cloud display and the cloud filter as they disagree.** `is_cloud` is `ZSTATE in (3, 6)`, so a cloud sample renders with the cloud glyph, but `--filter cloud` on `list recent` matches `ZSTATE = 3` only and `!cloud` matches `ZSTATE != 3`, so a cloud sample displays as cloud yet is excluded by the cloud filter. The 3-only filter is where the author's revert of an unauthorized 3-or-6 widening left it, reverted for landing before approval, not because the wider predicate was ruled wrong. Change neither side without his direction and a spec. Know what the specs pin: only that filtered rows are cloud, not the predicate's width, and the `!cloud` spec passes only because no fixture row sits at ZSTATE 6 with progress. `list all` accepts the cloud values and applies no cloud predicate; that is the current-state page's B-68.
18	- **B-48 — Treat the ZCONTENTTYPE mapping as unverified.** Likely 1 = book (EPUB), 3 = PDF. Every fixture row reads 1, so the fixtures cannot confirm the PDF half, and no spec pins either. Keep the doc's hedged wording in "Content Type Identification" and Domain Language; do not firm it up without a live query.
19	- **B-49 — Never use ZTITLE as a key.** One title can occupy several rows, at different ZSTATEs and even under two author strings for two editions. Handle duplicates explicitly in any title lookup, or detection becomes non-deterministic. The doc holds the iPhone screenshot showing two editions.
20	- **B-50 — Define finished as `ZISFINISHED = 1`, alone.** Finished books exist below 100% progress, so never require `ZREADINGPROGRESS = 1.0`. Know the fixture's shape before writing a not-finished predicate: it holds no finished book, and its unfinished rows carry NULL, not 0, in `ZISFINISHED`, so `= 0` or `!= 1` matches nothing there. No spec pins finished-ness yet; the library spec's finished-book TODO is where it lands.
21	- **B-51 — Leave `ZLASTOPENDATE` unguarded.** It was never seen NULL on a row with progress above 0, which is why `_row_to_book` converts it without a NULL check. The doc's NULL-timestamp warnings are speculation, not observations. Add or remove a guard only on live evidence and with a spec.
22	- **B-52 — Put sample listing on `list all`, not `list recent`.** Samples were never seen with `ZREADINGPROGRESS` above 0.0, and a sample's reading position was traced to a type-3 row in the AEAnnotation database instead; both facts are second-hand, from a relayed log analysis rather than a live probe. Because `list recent` filters on `ZREADINGPROGRESS > 0`, a sample filter there is structurally near-empty. The specs pin `list all`'s sample filter against the fixture's sample titles.
23	- **B-53 — Treat "Want to Read" as computed by Apple, not marked by the user.** Its observed composition is unread-or-sample: `ZREADINGPROGRESS = 0` and not finished, or a sample. Its ordering is unknown; do not reuse the recorded ZCREATIONDATE conclusion, which rests on an arithmetic error. Document observed database behavior, never inferred user intent, and write "unknown" where the mechanism is unknown.
24	
25	## The machine
26	
27	- **B-54 — Container lifecycle.** macOS creates `com.apple.iBooksX` at account setup; the first launch of Apple Books creates `com.apple.BKAgentService`, `Books.plist`, and an empty-table `BKLibrary-*.sqlite` together, with no Apple ID required; an older install can carry `Books.plist` with no `BKLibrary` directory at all. The fixture personas encode exactly these states, and `library.py` distinguishes a missing `BKLibrary` directory from an empty one with two different error messages; keep both paths specced. Reading another user's `~/Library` requires sudo, so a plain `--user <name>` run fails with PermissionError.
28	- **B-55 — Plist mechanics.** `Books.plist` stores `Books` as a list of dicts; `library.py` guards for list shape because a dict-keyed variant parses without error and yields zero books. Read it with `plistlib.load` on a binary-mode handle, which detects binary and XML itself; never shell out to `plutil -convert` from code. For exploration, render a plist as Swift literals with `plutil -convert swift -o out.swift Books.plist`, far cheaper in tokens than XML; the untracked `All_Books*.swift` dumps are such renderings.
29	- **B-56 — Path correlation is open; leave `path` empty.** `_row_to_book` sets `path=""` pending a `ZASSETID`-keyed correlation with `Books.plist`, and `path` is `NotRequired` on `Book` for the same reason. Whether the database offers a usable path column was never checked on a live library: the doc lists `ZPATH`, and in the fixture it holds an absolute `.epub` path on two local rows but NULL on the cloud rows and on one downloaded sample, so do not rely on it. This is design debt the author left as a TODO; do not resolve it as a drive-by.
30	
31	## Working the database
32	
33	- **B-57 — Query discipline.** Answer one-off questions with the `sqlite3` CLI directly: no throwaway scripts in the tree, no print-debugging through production code. Name columns, never `SELECT *`, because blurb columns flood the context. Pass titles as `?` parameters; hand-escaping apostrophes fails repeatedly. When a title with diacritics returns nothing, retry `LIKE` on its longest ASCII-only prefix before concluding the row is absent, because the shell round-trip, not the database, is what fails. Probe several items of one shape with a single `IN (...)`.
34	
35	## The doc's standing
36	
37	- **B-58 — How to read `docs/apple_books.md`.** It is the research spike's territory map, re-aligned with the project's recorded corrections where the record allowed. Read "Edge Cases and Special Considerations" and "UI Behavior Insights" as guesses written in the observational voice; read the rest as the observations this page compresses. Where this page and the doc differ, follow this page. Verify an attribute against a screenshot and a live query, never against the doc's prose alone.
38	- **B-59 — Editing rules for the doc.** Keep it descriptive of storage: no SQL that prescribes a feature's filtering strategy. Keep every SQL query in the single "Database to UI Mapping" section and link to it from elsewhere; two copies of one query is how the doc came to contradict itself. Document UI quirks, such as cloud samples rendered "1%", and never replicate them in code. Commit screenshots under `docs/ui/apple/` and reference each beside the claim it supports, labelled with the platform that produced it: iPhone tiles and macOS list views use different attribute vocabularies, and macOS "Complete" is a percentage, not a status. Preserve the existing segmentation when updating contents.
39	
40	## Further reading in `docs/apple_books.md`
41

43	- "Progress Data Sources Hierarchy": B-41

- Intel MacBook frozen on an older macOS: the natural cross-version control — same library, older Apple Books, so a schema difference between the two machines is a version difference and nothing else.

"""Apple Books library access functions."""

import datetime
import plistlib
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, NotRequired, TypedDict

from bookminder import BookminderError

APPLE_EPOCH = datetime.datetime(2001, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
APPLE_CONTAINERS = "Library/Containers/com.apple"

SUPPORTED_FILTERS = {"cloud", "!cloud", "sample", "!sample"}


def _books_plist(user_home: Path) -> Path:
    return (
        user_home
        / f"{APPLE_CONTAINERS}.BKAgentService/Data/Documents/iBooks/Books/Books.plist"
    )


def _get_bklibrary_db_file(user_home: Path) -> Path:
    bklibrary_path = user_home / f"{APPLE_CONTAINERS}.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary"
    if not bklibrary_path.exists():
        raise BookminderError(
            f"BKLibrary directory not found: {bklibrary_path}. "
            "Apple Books database not found."
        )

    db_files = list(bklibrary_path.glob("BKLibrary-*.sqlite"))
    if not db_files:
        raise BookminderError(
            f"No BKLibrary database found in: {bklibrary_path}. "
            "Apple Books database not found."
        )

    return db_files[0]


class Book(TypedDict):
    """Book metadata from Apple Books library."""

    title: str
    author: str
    path: NotRequired[str]
    updated: NotRequired[datetime.datetime]
    reading_progress_percentage: NotRequired[int]
    is_cloud: NotRequired[bool]
    is_sample: NotRequired[bool]


def _get_user_path(user: str | None) -> Path:
    """Convert user parameter to Path."""
    if user:
        user_path = Path(user)
        if not user_path.is_absolute():
            user_path = Path(f"/Users/{user}")
    else:
        user_path = Path.home()
    return user_path


def _apple_timestamp_to_datetime(timestamp: float) -> datetime.datetime:
    return APPLE_EPOCH + datetime.timedelta(seconds=timestamp)


def _row_to_book(row: sqlite3.Row) -> Book:
    return Book(
        title=row["ZTITLE"] or "Unknown",
        author=row["ZAUTHOR"] or "Unknown",
        path="",  # Path requires Books.plist correlation with ZASSETID
        updated=_apple_timestamp_to_datetime(row["ZLASTOPENDATE"]),
        reading_progress_percentage=int(row["ZREADINGPROGRESS"] * 100),
        is_cloud=row["ZSTATE"] in (3, 6),
        is_sample=row["ZSTATE"] == 6 or row["ZISSAMPLE"] == 1,
    )


def _read_books_plist(user_home: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    books_plist = _books_plist(user_home)
    with open(books_plist, "rb") as f:
        plist_data = plistlib.load(f)
    books = plist_data.get("Books", [])
    return books if isinstance(books, list) else []


def list_books(user_home: Path) -> list[Book]:
    """List books from the Apple Books library."""
    raw_books = _read_books_plist(user_home)

    books: list[Book] = [
        Book(
            title=book.get("itemName", "Unknown"),
            path=book.get("path", ""),
            author=book.get("artistName", "Unknown"),
            updated=book.get("updateDate", datetime.datetime.min),
        )
        for book in raw_books
    ]
    return books


def find_book_by_title(title: str, user_home: Path) -> Book | None:
    """Find a book by exact title match."""
    return next(
        (book for book in list_books(user_home) if book["title"] == title), None
    )


def _build_books_query(where_clause: str = "", limit: int | None = None) -> str:
    """Build SQL query for fetching books from BKLibrary database."""
    query = f"""
        SELECT ZTITLE, ZAUTHOR, ZREADINGPROGRESS, ZLASTOPENDATE, ZSTATE, ZISSAMPLE
        FROM ZBKLIBRARYASSET
        {where_clause}
        ORDER BY ZLASTOPENDATE DESC
    """

    if limit:
        query += f" LIMIT {limit}"

    return query


def _query_books(
    user_home: Path,
    where_clause: str = "",
    params: tuple = (),
    limit: int | None = None,
) -> list[Book]:
    """Query books from BKLibrary database with optional WHERE clause."""
    db_file = _get_bklibrary_db_file(user_home)

    with sqlite3.connect(db_file) as conn:
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        cursor = conn.cursor()

        query = _build_books_query(where_clause, limit)
        cursor.execute(query, params)
        rows = cursor.fetchall()

        return [_row_to_book(row) for row in rows]


def list_recent_books(user: str | None = None, filter: str | None = None) -> list[Book]:
    """List recently read books with progress from BKLibrary database."""
    user_home = _get_user_path(user)
    try:
        where_parts = ["WHERE ZREADINGPROGRESS > 0"]
        params = []

        if filter == "cloud":
            where_parts.append("AND ZSTATE = ?")
            params.append(3)
        elif filter == "!cloud":
            where_parts.append("AND ZSTATE != ?")
            params.append(3)
        elif filter == "sample":
            where_parts.append("AND (ZSTATE = 6 OR ZISSAMPLE = 1)")
        elif filter == "!sample":
            where_parts.append("AND ZSTATE != 6 AND ZISSAMPLE != 1")

        where_clause = " ".join(where_parts)
        return _query_books(user_home, where_clause, tuple(params), limit=10)
    except sqlite3.Error as e:
        raise BookminderError(f"Error reading Apple Books database: {e}") from e


def list_all_books(user: str | None = None, filter: str | None = None) -> list[Book]:
    """List all books from BKLibrary database."""
    user_home = _get_user_path(user)

    where_clause = ""
    if filter == "sample":
        where_clause = "WHERE (ZSTATE = 6 OR ZISSAMPLE = 1)"
    elif filter == "!sample":
        where_clause = "WHERE ZSTATE != 6 AND ZISSAMPLE != 1"

    return _query_books(user_home, where_clause)

    func = click.option(

        default=None,
        help="Examine books for specified user (default: current user)",
    )(func)
    func = click.option(
        "--filter",
        default=None,
        help="Filter books by attribute (cloud, !cloud, sample, !sample, etc).",
    )(func)
    return func

    progress = book.get("reading_progress_percentage")
    progress_str = f" ({progress}%)" if progress is not None else ""
    sample_str = " • Sample" if book.get("is_sample") else ""
    cloud_str = " ☁️" if book.get("is_cloud") else ""
    return f"{book['title']} - {book['author']}{progress_str}{sample_str}{cloud_str}"


def format_book_list(books: list[Book], empty_message: str = "No books found") -> str:
    """Format a list of books for display."""
    if not books:

    return "\n".join(format(book) for book in books)

    try:
        books = list_all_books(user=user, filter=filter)
        click.echo(format_book_list(books))

Read the section for any store, column, or user state before writing code or a spec that touches it. What a spec pins against the fixtures is established; what this page calls unknown is a boundary, not a gap to fill by reasoning from the UI or from prose. ## What exists on disk

Apple Books keeps one library in two sandboxed containers under `~/Library/Containers/`:

- `com.apple.BKAgentService/Data/Documents/iBooks/Books/` holds `Books.plist` and the downloaded book files, one `<asset-id>.epub` per downloaded book.
- `com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/` holds the library database, `BKLibrary-*.sqlite`. Find it by that glob, never by literal name: the numeric segments in the file name differ per install.

The database is the library; the plist and the `.epub` files describe what has been downloaded from it. Books lazy-download from iCloud, so a library row with no `.epub` on disk is a normal row: presence on disk is a download state, never a membership test, and no code path stats a book file.

Two further stores are known only at arm's length. A relayed log analysis, never a live probe, traced a sample's reading position to a type-3 row holding an `epubcfi` location in an AEAnnotation database (`AEAnnotation_v10312011_1727_local.sqlite`); its location and schema were never examined. A `BCRecentlyOpenedBooksDB` store is claimed as well, with nothing in the record confirming or correcting it. Treat both as unmapped.

## Books.plist

The plist catalogues the BKAgentService container: a dict whose `Books` key holds a list of dicts, one per entry. Take from an entry `itemName`, `artistName`, `path`, `updateDate`, and `itemId`, the asset id that also names the entry's `.epub` file. It is the store the code reads file paths from, which is why `list_books` and `find_book_by_title` stay in the tree as the seed of the EPUB content path, a ruling the current-state page holds.

Do not read reading state or membership from it. Its only progress field, `BKPercentComplete`, appears on finished books alone and always as 1.0, so it cannot express progress. Take recency from the database's `ZLASTOPENDATE`.

Read the plist with `plistlib.load` on a binary-mode handle, which detects binary and XML itself; never shell out to `plutil -convert` from code. Treat the mapping as unverified: likely 1 = book (EPUB), 3 = PDF. Every fixture row reads 1, so the fixtures cannot confirm the PDF half, and no spec pins either. Keep the doc's hedged wording; do not firm it up without a live query.
